claims.statement: After their own failure (being told their answer was wrong), people learn as much as after a success.
claims.exposure: failure feedback on one's own answers (told « wrong »)
claims.comparison: success feedback on one's own answers (told « right »)
claims.outcome: learning: score on a later test of the same information, or later performance

claims.statement: Making errors while learning, when an explanation follows (trying a problem before being taught), leads to better understanding and transfer than being taught first.
claims.population: learners from secondary school to university
claims.exposure: trying a problem and making errors first, then instruction
claims.outcome: understanding and transfer to new tasks after the training (not routine procedures)

claims.statement: People learn from other people's failures at least as much as from other people's successes.
claims.outcome: learning: later test score, or later performance

claims.statement: The more one fails, the more likely one is to succeed: a setback leads to better results later.
claims.population: adults and students pursuing a goal (career, grants, exams)
claims.exposure: a failure or setback (a near miss)
claims.outcome: later performance and success; staying in the pursuit

notFound: no sample from Egypt; the only Arab-world sample is one small Saudi school quasi-experiment of productive failure (ezzeldin-2022-saudi, c2 only, high risk of bias); Sinha 2021 pools Saudi comparisons in « Asia » with no separate estimate

no replication of « people learn less from their own failure » outside the Script Task of Eskreis-Winkler & Fishbach, and no multi-lab replication: both replications (Keith 2022, Gok 2024) use the same task

Spiller 2025 (10.1177/09567976251333666, Psychological Science, commentary with a preregistered experiment) and the authors' reply (10.1177/09567976251391180): both typed « editorial » by OpenAlex, so the verifier refuses them as notices; read in their abstracts, written as limits of the three sheets that use the task

Traag et al. 2025 (10.7554/elife.109042, eLife reviewed preprint, replication of Wang 2019 across 14 programmes): Crossref « posted-content », the verifier would only give « review »; written as a limit of wang-2019-setback

no meta-analysis comparing learning after one's own failure with learning after success; no meta-analysis of error management training after Keith & Frese 2008; no independent meta-analysis of productive failure (Darabi 2018 and Ashman 2019: no abstract anywhere; Chen & Kalyuga 2019: abstract without a result, per the counter-evidence review)
pretesting meta-analyses (King-Shepard 2025, Yan 2025): no abstract found by the counter-evidence review; not added

Yin et al. 2019 (Nature, dynamics of failure): its correction concerns only figure axes (read by the counter-evidence review), so the draft's reason to leave it out falls; still not added: a model tested on observational data, indirect for c4, kept for the evidence page

recent small trials named by the counter-evidence review (productive failure: Braas 2025, Loibl & Leuders 2024, Trninic 2022; error management: Davenport & Beier 2024, Meritet 2021, Aliaga 2024, Dyre 2016) not added as sheets: mixed results, none changes the direction of c2; read on the evidence page

Eskreis-Winkler et al. 2024 (people overestimate recovery after a failure) and Klein Teeselink 2023 (« losing leads to winning » not replicated in sports): not added, indirect for c4 (beliefs; sports half-time)
Taha et al. 2025 (370 Egyptian nursing students, cross-sectional: failure appraisal and helplessness): not added, it does not test learning nor later success
the book's ch. 7 itself not read (no copy; Goodreads highlight pages blocked): the basis is the author's own page « 20 Paradoxes That Are True » (2013)
Bol 2018: number of applicants near the funding threshold (SI appendix: the PMC copy answers with an anti-robot page, Europe PMC with 403; not circumvented): no n on the sheet
Lin-Siegler 2016: full text not read (PsycNet and the Columbia repository answer with an application or an anti-robot page): level of random assignment unknown, `experiment` provisional
Loh 2012: full text closed, no open repository: the contradiction of its abstract on personality is not resolved; only ability is used

found.note: Spiller 2025, Psychological Science, preregistered: the Script Task's scoring makes the « less from failure » gap without any feedback; refused by the verifier (OpenAlex « editorial »): c1 becomes insufficient, never said, not even as a question

Eskreis-Winkler & Fishbach 2025 reply: consistency explains the effect « in some paradigms », not in theirs; no new data in the abstract: the debate is open, written in the limits of the three sheets that use the task
same task; the exact MTurk comparison (1b) is small and not significant; Study 3 not randomized (with-instruction now an association); no ego-threat difference: the ego explanation is never said
« with corrective feedback the gap disappears » is also what the artefact predicts: it cannot carry the nuance, which moves to c2 (Sinha 2021, Alfieri 2011)

added: discovering alone does worse than explicit teaching (d = -0.38), supported discovery better (d = 0.26 against direct teaching): the two halves of ⚖️ and the nuance; not on screen, discovery is not failure

added: encouraging errors beat forbidding them but not a neutral training, earlier gains put on confounds: the error-training strand drops to low and leaves c2, narrowed to « try first, then the explanation »

Braas 2025, with Loibl & Leuders 2024 and Trninic 2022: recent null replications of productive failure; not added, no second step down: small trials around a moderate, heterogeneous effect whose conditions are in the claim
Kirschner 2006, Kessels 2003, Wong 2026: guidance first is better for novices and impaired learners; c2's population starts at secondary school; the « for whom » goes to the evidence page
Traag 2025, eLife reviewed preprint, 14 programmes: Wang's setback advantage is not robust and likely a selection of who reapplies; a limit of wang-2019-setback, a nuance only
added: narrow losers of an early grant gathered less than half the funding of narrow winners over eight years, partly because they applied less: c4 contradicted
added: 49,231 pupils in England: just failing the grade meant fewer high tracks, less higher education, more dropout at 18: c4 contradicted, same rank as Wang
Eskreis-Winkler et al. 2024: people overestimate recovery after a failure (survivorship); with Klein Teeselink 2023 (« losing leads to winning » not replicated in sports): indirect for c4, not added
added for c3, then a nuance only (second blind review): stories of hardship without any failure did as well as stories of mistakes, and the outcome is learning through motivation
Fishbach 2026, short review by the original author: failure teaches more than instruction alone; low rank, it would go with c2; not added
Butowska-Buczynska 2024: the errorful-learning advantage disappears when study time is equated; with Wong 2023 (small, one lab): evidence page, not added
the only Arab sample: 66 Saudi pupils, one school per group, no pretest reported, eta² ≈ 0.8: high risk of bias, it carries nothing; the applicability line is written
Taha 2025, 370 Egyptian nursing students, cross-sectional: negative failure appraisal goes with helplessness; tests neither learning nor later success: not added

counterEvidence.conclusion: ⚖️ low holds; ❌ is not defensible. Taken: c1 insufficient (one contested task, Spiller 2025), never said; c2 narrowed to « try first, then the explanation », moderate (Sinha, Alfieri), error training low (Loh); c3 low, a question at most; c4 contradicted, low (Bol, Machin; Wang not robust, Traag). Refused: a second step down for c2; Alfieri on screen (discovery is not failure): Sinha.
